items.title: Example 5.17 · The actual sphere Rayleigh Hessian

source.anchor: §5.5, Corollary 5.16 and Example 5.17 (printed p. 96 / PDF p. 112)
source.attribution: Nicolas Boumal. ASTIS-authored restatement and solution; no source prose, figures, or PDF redistributed. The source PDF is marked free for personal use only.

items.statement: For the half-normalized symmetric Rayleigh quadratic on a finite-dimensional Euclidean unit sphere, the induced gradient is Ax−⟨x,Ax⟩x. Differentiate its smooth ambient extension and project to the tangent plane. On a tangent vector u the Hessian is Pₓ(Au)−⟨x,Ax⟩u.
assumptions: A is a symmetric continuous real-linear operator and x lies on the unit sphere in finite-dimensional E.
The chart parameter n satisfies dim E=n+1, permitting n=0. The inner product is the ambient one pulled back along the actual sphere inclusion.

obligations.label: Define the exact smooth gradient extension.
Use the tangent subtype for both input and output of the projected derivative.
Identify the extension with the genuine induced gradient of the half quadratic.
Differentiate the extension and project to obtain the exact Hessian operator and quadratic form.

bindings.boundary: A named polynomial definition. Differentiability and actual gradient identity are separate proofs.

assumption_deltas.source: The example uses the polynomial extension for symmetric matrices in finite Euclidean space.
assumption_deltas.lean: The polynomial itself is defined on every real inner-product space for any continuous linear A.
assumption_deltas.reason: The definition does not assert it is the gradient away from the source's symmetric unit-sphere setting.

bindings.boundary: A concrete tangent operator construction for any continuous real-linear A. It is identified with the actual induced Hessian in the finite-dimensional symmetric source setting only. No general connection or derivative-existence claim follows from the definition.

assumption_deltas.source: For the finite-dimensional symmetric half quadratic, the source projects the derivative of the actual gradient extension and acts only on tangent directions.
assumption_deltas.lean: For any continuous real-linear A on a real inner-product space, compose tangent inclusion, fderiv of the stated polynomial and orthogonal projection.
assumption_deltas.reason: Both domain and codomain are the actual tangent plane. Genuine differentiability and the identification with the source's induced gradient Hessian are separate; there is no general nonsymmetric Hessian claim.

bindings.boundary: The gradient pairing is for the actual restricted half quadratic; no Hessian conclusion is made here.

assumption_deltas.source: The half-normalized symmetric quadratic with the induced metric on a finite Euclidean sphere.
assumption_deltas.lean: A symmetric continuous linear A, finite-dimensional E and dim E=n+1, with actual manifold differentiability and inclusion pairing.
assumption_deltas.reason: Coordinate-free Euclidean types preserve the source hypotheses. The chart dimension is bookkeeping, not an extra positive-dimensional tangent requirement.

bindings.boundary: The displayed formula for the actual projected derivative. The finite-dimensional symmetric source identification uses a separate gradient pairing; the general calculation does not claim an objective Hessian for arbitrary A.

assumption_deltas.source: The Hessian formula is given for the symmetric quadratic on the finite Euclidean sphere.
assumption_deltas.lean: The projected derivative formula is computed for arbitrary continuous real-linear A on a real inner-product space.
assumption_deltas.reason: Only the extension derivative and projection are generalized. The actual gradient interpretation still uses the separate symmetry-dependent identity.

items.title: Exercise 5.18 · Stationarity and tangent PSD imply global optimality

source.anchor: §5.5, Exercise 5.18 continuing Example 5.17 (printed p. 96 / PDF p. 112)
source.attribution: Nicolas Boumal. ASTIS-authored restatement and solution; no source prose, figures, or PDF redistributed. The source PDF is marked free for personal use only.

items.statement: For a real symmetric operator on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, restrict the half-normalized quadratic to the unit sphere with its induced metric. If the sphere gradient at a unit point x is zero and the induced Hessian is positive semidefinite on every tangent direction there, then x minimizes the restriction globally and is a nonzero eigenvector at the least eigenvalue of the operator.
assumptions: E is finite-dimensional and real with its inner-product norm; A is symmetric and x is a unit sphere point.
The Hessian is the induced tangent operator of Example 5.17. PSD holds on every tangent direction, including zero. No eigengap, simple spectrum, or ambient PSD is assumed.

formulae.label: Source conclusion
formulae.tex: G(x)=0,\quad \langle u,H_xu\rangle\ge0\ (u\perp x)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(x)\le F(y)\ (\|y\|=1),\quad Ax=\lambda x,\quad \lambda=\min\operatorname{eig}(A).

formulae.label: The objective gap is a tangent quadratic form
formulae.tex: \begin{aligned}a&=\langle x,y\rangle,\quad u=y-ax,\quad a^2+\|u\|^2=1,\\ 2(F(y)-F(x))&=a^2\lambda+\langle u,Au\rangle-\lambda\\&=\langle u,Au\rangle-\lambda\|u\|^2=\langle u,H_xu\rangle\ge0.\end{aligned}

obligations.label: Use tangent PSD at stationarity to prove global minimization and an attained least eigenvalue.

bindings.boundary: Only the named sphere quadratic exercise: global comparison, attainment, and leastness. No gap, uniqueness, arbitrary manifold sufficiency, or chapter completion.

assumption_deltas.source: Stationary induced gradient and PSD induced Hessian at a unit point imply global minimality and smallest-eigenvalue membership.
assumption_deltas.lean: The certified ambient gradient representative vanishes; PSD is quantified on every actual tangent u. IsMinOn and HasEigenvector plus leastness are separate conclusions.
assumption_deltas.reason: The pairing certificate identifies the stationary hypothesis and the Hessian is the actual projected gradient derivative. Unit membership supplies the nonzero eigenvector; no hidden spectral premise.
